EventDisplay.Name: Christmas by the Lake
EventDisplay.Description:
Welcome to the Award-Winning Christmas by the Lake in Clear Lake, Iowa: Join us in celebrating the holiday spirit at Clear Lake's Christmas by the Lake event, a holiday festival that's won several regional and statewide awards. Spanning the first weekend in December, this family-friendly festival promises a fun-filled variety of activities for all ages. Come to Clear Lake and create cherished holiday memories with your loved ones.

Festival Highlights:

Thursday:

  • Lights on 5K (5:30 PM)
    One Vision's Kinney-Lindstrom Center (1200 N 9th St W)
    Kick off the festivities with One Vision's 11th Annual Lights on 5K Run/Walk. Participants are encouraged to dress in festive costumes and lights. All proceeds from registrations and donations are used to buy holiday gifts for individuals with disabilities supported by One Vision. Register today at lightson5k.org and support a great cause.
  • Candy Cane Fun Run (5:45 PM)
    One Vision's Kinney-Lindstrom Center (1200 N 9th St W)
    Kids will have a chance to run with Santa and Mrs. Claus along the North Drive of One Vision's main campus. Every participant will receive a commemorative medal to celebrate their achievement. Register at lightson5k.org.

Friday:

  • Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony (5:30 PM)
    Clear Lake City Park Bandshell
    Join us to kick off Christmas by the Lake weekend with a tree lighting ceremony in City Park. This year we are collecting donations for the Clear Lake Food Bank. Bring to the tree lighting or drop off at the Chamber in advance.

Saturday:

  • Holiday Photo Opportunity (All Day)
    Clear Lake City Park Bandshell
    Snag a photo in front of a perfect Christmas backdrop.
  • Breakfast with Santa (7:30-10 AM)
    St. Patrick's Catholic Church (1101 9th Ave S)
    Presented by the Knights of Columbus along with the Boy Scouts. Enjoy pancakes, sausage, milk, juice, and coffee provided by Cabin Coffee! $5 per person, no advance ticket sales, pay at the door. Santa will be available from 7:30-9:30 AM for photos.
  • Holiday Bazaar & Vendor Market (9 AM-3 PM)
    Clear Lake Middle School (1601 3rd Ave N)
    Wind through rows of your favorite vendors in the Clear Lake Middle School gymnasium. Enjoy donuts and coffee in the morning and a sloppy joe meal deal for $5 in the afternoon. Don't miss the bake sale and door prizes. All proceeds from the bake sale will benefit the high school band trip.
  • Jingle and Arts Jubilee: Arts Center Holiday Open House (9 AM-5 PM)
    Clear Lake Arts Center (17 S 4th St)
    Get ahead start on your holiday shopping with unique, handcrafted gifts and art pieces. Enjoy a festive day with seasonal treats, and an opportunity to meet the artisans behind the creations.
  • C.A.R.E.S. Christmas by the Lake BINGO (10 AM-3 PM)
    VFW (219 Main Ave)
    Join the C.A.R.E.S. team for a festive round of BINGO. Proceeds help create a safe and memorable prom night for Clear Lake students.
  • Pizza & Photos with the Grinch & Cindy Lou Who (10AM-3PM)
    Lakeview Room (10 N Lakeview Drive)
    Meet the iconic Grinch and the adorable Cindy Lou Who for an unforgettable photo opportunity and pizza. All proceeds benefit the Clear Lake Dance Team.
  • Prince & Princess Crowning (10:15 AM)
    Clear Lake Bank & Trust (322 Main Avenue)
    Join us as we crown 2024's Christmas by the Lake Prince and Princess.
  • Story Time for Ages 3-6 (2 Sessions: 10:15 AM & 11:30 AM)
    Clear Lake Public Library (200 N 4th St)
    Story Time will be held at 10:15 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. in the meeting room, featuring festive stories, songs, and a craft. A hot cocoa bar will be set up to enjoy. Children must be accompanied by an adult.
  • Live Cello and Piano (11:30 AM-2:30 PM)
    Holistic Harmony (313 N 8th St)
    Stop in for a tea latte and enjoy beautiful live cello and piano music that may bring a tear to your eye.
  • Christmas Karaoke & S'mores (1-4 PM)
    Zion Dock Overhang (500 Main Avenue)
    Join Mojo Productions and show off your singing skills. Don't forget to enjoy a delicious s'more.
  • FSB Warming House (1-4 PM)
    Farmers State Bank (210 1st Ave N)
    Get out of the cold and enjoy warm drinks and popcorn inside Farmers State Bank.
  • Horse Drawn Carriage, Horse Drawn Wagon and Tractor Pulled Hayrack Rides (1-4 PM)
    Boarding locations: Wilcox Furniture (418 Main Ave) and Ge-Jo's (12 N 3rd St)
    Enjoy a fun ride around Clear Lake's downtown district.
  • Petting Zoo & Pony Rides (1-4 PM)
    Clear Lake City Park
    Pet your favorite furry friend or take a spin on a small pony ride.
  • Visit with Santa (1-4 PM & 6-7 PM)
    Santa's House in Clear Lake City Park
    Tell Santa exactly what's on your Christmas list. Don't forget to snag a photo with your camera or mobile device!
  • Professor Von Air Balloon Artist (1-4 PM)
    Zion on Main (500 Main Avenue)
    Have Professor Von Air make the perfect balloon creation for your little one.
  • Zion on Main Activities (1-4 PM)
    Zion on Main (500 Main Avenue)
    Activities include inflatables, live entertainment, 9-square, Gaga Ball, and photos with Super Mario and Bluey, plus a warming house and hot cocoa.
  • Card Making (1-4 PM)
    Clear Lake Public Library (200 N 4th St)
    Join us as we transform our meeting room to a Christmas card making workshop.  Create cards to send to friends and family with stamps and embellishments. A hot cocoa bar will be set up to enjoy while you create.
  • Lighted Parade and Spectacular Fireworks Finale (5:07 PM)
    Clear Lake Main Avenue & Seawall
    The lighted parade begins at 8th Street & Main Avenue and will travel toward the lake, turning north along N Lakeview Drive. The Fireworks display will begin after the parade.

Sunday:

  • Polar Bear Plunge presented by Clear Lake Jaycees (10:30 AM-1:30 PM)
    Clear Lake City Beach
    10:30 AM: Check-in/Registration and pre-party for Plungers at the VFW in Clear Lake. All participants will receive a BOGO token to enjoy a cocktail or beer.
    12:00 PM: Check-in/Registration moves to the Yacht Club
    12:30 PM: Plungers take the plunge!
    1:00 PM: Warming Party at Tap'd (Tap'd will have a live band to enjoy!)
    Warming tents will be onsite to change afterwards. When you check-in, you can provide your team name in order to be announced to plunge together. Fun costumes or outfits encouraged but not required. Registration is a donation to the local Toys for Tots + Clear Lake Kids & Families In Need Fund. A minimum donation of $60 will get you 2024 Polar Bear Plunge (navy blue crew neck) Sweatshirt. Want the sweet shirt but not wanting to fully commit to jumping in the lake? Join our Toe Dippers Club. You still get the swag, still get to attend the pre-party/post-party, still get the cold sensation with a tip of your foot, and our charities still get your support, its win-win-win. If you would like to donate and not dip, feel free to Venmo us at @ClearLake-Jaycees.
  • Visit with Santa (1-4 PM)
    Santa's House in City Park
    Tell Santa exactly what's on your Christmas list. Don't forget to snag a photo with your camera or mobile device!

Why Visit Christmas by the Lake?

  • Family-Friendly Fun: From petting zoos and pony rides to visits with Santa and Mrs. Claus, there's something for everyone.
  • Local Culture: Experience the best of Clear Lake with our unique blend of holiday traditions and modern entertainment.
  • Stunning Scenery: Enjoy the beauty of a frozen lake and the charm of our decorated town.

Stay updated!

For the latest schedule updates and event details, visit our website frequently. Don't miss out on any of the holiday fun at Clear Lake's Christmas by the Lake!

Join Us for a Magical Holiday Experience!

EventDisplay.Name: Chris Funk: The Wonderist – Redefining Wonder
EventDisplay.Description: Chris Funk’s REDEFINING WONDER is an engaging multimedia experience that has audiences talking and scratching their heads for years to come. From NBC’s America’s Got Talent, CW’s Penn & Teller: Fool Us & Masters of Illusion, FOX’s Hell’s Kitchen and Syfy’s Wizard Wars, Chris has pioneered the use of instruments like the violin, guitar and more into his show. Chris tells his story on how he integrated his love for music and magic in a show unlike any other. A mesmerizing violin concerto that brings objects to life, paired with a hypnotic guitar loop that transforms sound into magic, his show is in a league of its own. The live-feed camera and interactive videos bring audiences up onstage and into the action, delivering a show that family audiences will treasure.

EventDisplay.Name: Jim Brickman: A Christmas Celebration LIVE!
EventDisplay.Description: Jim Brickman’s A Christmas Celebration is a holiday concert event filled with music, laughter and beautiful moments that last a lifetime. Be a part of the magic and join audiences, of all ages, who call it their favorite Yuletide tradition. Some even say it’s “The best Christmas show ever.” Grab your seats and find out for yourself! Jim Brickman’s distinctive piano style and captivating live performances have revolutionized the popularity of instrumental music, making him a driving force behind modern American music. The hit-making songwriter is the best-selling solo pianist of our time, earning 22 Number One albums, 32 Top 20 Radio Singles, two Grammy® nominations, and Gospel Music’s Dove Award. Hope, faith, and peace are truly at the heart of Jim Brickman’s passionate songwriting.

EventDisplay.Name: Emmet Cahill: Christmas in Ireland
EventDisplay.Description: After an unforgettable evening with Celtic Thunder last season, we are thrilled to welcome Emmet Cahill back to NIACC for the holidays, joined by Seamus Brett and a string quartet. Experience stunning renditions of your favorite Christmas carols, including O Holy Night, Adeste Fideles, I’ll Be Home for Christmas, Silent Night, and more. Emmet Cahill: Christmas in Ireland will take you on a musical journey to Ireland, featuring beloved carols, Christmas stories from the Emerald Isle, and Irish classics such as Danny Boy, An Irish Lullaby, and When Irish Eyes Are Smiling. A star of the PBS phenomenon Celtic Thunder, Emmet Cahill sold out his debut solo performance at New York’s Carnegie Hall and has appeared with the world-famous Tabernacle Choir. He is quickly earning a reputation as one of the leading voices of his generation.

EventDisplay.Name: Book Chat: To the Moon and Back
EventDisplay.Description: Book Chat meets on the third Tuesday of every month at 12:00 pm in the library meeting room. To the Moon and Back by Eliana Ramage: Steph Harper is convinced that only space—outer space—can save her. From a childhood of fearful running and alienation; from a family and community that threaten to suffocate her with their reverence for the past. Equal parts tender, funny, and heartbreaking, To the Moon and Back charts the course of Steph’s singular dream: to become the first Cherokee astronaut, no matter who or what she has to leave behind. But despite her self-prescribed loneliness and reckless ambition, Steph’s story isn’t hers alone. To the Moon and Back also brings to life the vibrant, complex women—a celebrity activist younger sister, an ex-Mormon college girlfriend, and a devoted mother with a crushing secret—who insist on loving her…even when she least deserves them. From a simulated Mars habitat on a Hawaiian volcano, to a house in the Ozark foothills in Cherokee Nation, to a pressurized research station on the floor of the Atlantic and beyond, Steph will stretch her bonds with each of these women to the point of breaking, driving them to reconsider their own deepest desires in her shadow. An awe-inspiringly epic novel of mothers and daughters, sisters and sacrifice, love and loss, terror and wonder, To the Moon and Back is the unforgettable story of one astronaut’s most surprising discovery: how deeply she loves life on earth.
EventDisplay.LocationDesc: Clear Lake Public Library 200 N 4th St

EventDisplay.Name: Books on Tap: This is How I Lied
EventDisplay.Description: Books on Tap meets on the third Wednesday of every month at 6:00 pm at Lake Time Brewery. This is How I Lied by Heather Gudenkauf: Twenty-five years ago, the body of sixteen-year-old Eve Knox was found in the caves near her home in small-town Grotto, Iowa—discovered by her best friend, Maggie, and her sister, Nola. There were a handful of suspects, including her boyfriend, Nick, but without sufficient evidence the case ultimately went cold. For decades Maggie was haunted by Eve’s death and that horrible night. Now a detective in Grotto, and seven months pregnant, she is thrust back into the past when a new piece of evidence surfaces and the case is reopened. As Maggie investigates and reexamines the clues, secrets about what really happened begin to emerge. But someone in town knows more than they’re letting on, and they’ll stop at nothing to keep the truth buried deep.

EventDisplay.Name: Hawkeye Tailgate For The Kids
EventDisplay.Description: On November 21, the Lovell Family will host Hawkeye Tailgate for the Kids at The Palms in Clear Lake, Iowa, bringing together Hawkeye football, community, and a cause incredibly close to our hearts. Proceeds from the event will support pediatric cancer research at the University of Iowa, including the work of Dr. Jessica Zimmerman, Adeline’s pediatric oncologist. The event will feature Dr. Jessica Zimmerman, Adeline’s pediatric oncologist; Regent Steve Lacy of the Iowa Board of Regents; and the Lovell family, sharing more about Adeline’s journey and the importance of pediatric cancer research during Halftime. The event time is dependent on the Hawkeye game time announcement. All proceeds from Hawkeye Tailgate for the Kids will support Dr. Zimmerman’s pediatric cancer research through the Pediatric Leukemia Research Fund at UI Health Care Stead Family Children’s Hospital. To purchase tickets or sponsorships, contact Morgan Lovell at morganlovell@cltel.com. You can donate to the event at https://uigoldrush.org/wavesrise. Our daughter, Adeline Lovell, was four years old when she was diagnosed with high-risk B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in July 2022. For the next two and a half years, the University of Iowa Stead Family Children’s Hospital became our second home. Her journey brought plenty of hard days, including a severe anaphylactic reaction to one of her chemotherapy drugs that required an alternative treatment and even more time in Iowa City. But somehow, there was also so much joy along the way. There was The Wave. Meeting Caitlin Clark. Glorifying God on stage at a Rend Collective concert. And eventually, an incredible full-circle moment when the little girl who had once waved from the hospital windows became an Iowa Football Kid Captain, standing inside Kinnick Stadium and waving back. In November 2024, after two and a half years of treatment, Adeline finished chemotherapy. Our family will never forget the doctors, nurses, and staff who helped get her there. In February 2026, we shared our story in Waves Rise: A Mother’s Story of Childhood Cancer and Unshakeable Faith. Now, this tailgate is another opportunity to give back and help fund the research that gives children like Adeline more tomorrows.
EventDisplay.LocationDesc: The Palms, Clear Lake

EventDisplay.Name: Great White Concert
EventDisplay.Description: For a band to continue to thrive 40 years in the music business, the mantra must be, these songs are bigger than any one member. GRAMMY nominated hard rock legends Great White are adding onto that line with the saying: expect the unexpected. It’s rock and roll, baby. The peaks and the valleys haven’t stopped– nor has the music. Great White’s ride runs deep and its passion for the music goes beyond any depth. Four decades in and Great White enlists Brett Carlisle to take over vocal duties and lead the charge on hit after hit. That arsenal of songs include the Grammy nominated Best Hard Rock Performance hit, “Once Bitten, Twice Shy,” Great White has sold over 10 million albums worldwide, has six Top 100 Billboard hits, nine Top 200 Billboard albums, two platinum albums, and clocked the top of MTV four times. To experience their hits live in concert—“Rock Me,” “Mista Bone,” “Save Your Love,” “House of Broken Love,” and “Lady Red Light”—is to ride an emotional wave of sultry connections, arousing lyrics, and an all-out marathon of hard-hitting orchestrations. Audiences might also hear tracks like “Stick It”, “The Angel Song”, “Big Time” or one of the many deep cuts from Great White’s 13 studio albums. California-based Great White is Mark Kendall (guitar), Michael Lardie (guitar, keyboards), Audie Desbrow (drums), Scott Snyder (bass), and Brett Carlisle (vocals). Since 1982, the Great White sound has captivated audiences worldwide with crushing, blues-based guitar riffs and swagger that invokes an emotional high for anyone that listens. The band’s core writing team of Lardie and Kendall forged numerous hits over the years, and when Desbrow joined in ’85, the grooves hooked an amazing stride. Great White 2022 2 Now for more than a decade, Snyder has merged his unforgiving rhythm to Desbrow’s relentless percussion. Carlisle, born and raised in Alabama, brings a Southern rock charm laced with Bayou blue-based grit. From an early gig at the famed Los Angeles’ Troubadour, to sharing arena stages with rock’s biggest names like Judas Priest, Whitesnake, Scorpions, to globe-trotting alongside contemporaries Slaughter, Vixen, Skid Row, Vince Neil and more – Great White continues to bring its exhilarating live performance to the masses.

EventDisplay.Name: Mystery Book Club: The Boys from Biloxi
EventDisplay.Description: The Mystery Book Club meets on the first Tuesday of the month at 6:00 pm in the library. The Boys from Biloxi by John Grisham: For most of the last hundred years, Biloxi was known for its beaches, resorts, and seafood industry. But it had a darker side. It was also notorious for corruption and vice, everything from gambling, prostitution, bootleg liquor, and drugs to contract killings. The vice was controlled by small cabal of mobsters, many of them rumored to be members of the Dixie Mafia. Keith Rudy and Hugh Malco grew up in Biloxi in the sixties and were childhood friends, as well as Little League all-stars. But as teenagers, their lives took them in different directions. Keith’s father became a legendary prosecutor, determined to “clean up the Coast.” Hugh’s father became the “Boss” of Biloxi’s criminal underground. Keith went to law school and followed in his father’s footsteps. Hugh preferred the nightlife and worked in his father’s clubs. The two families were headed for a showdown—one that would ultimately happen in a courtroom.

EventDisplay.Name: Book Chat: The Correspondent
EventDisplay.Description: Book Chat meets on the third Tuesday of every month at 12:00 pm in the library meeting room. The Correspondent by Virginia Evans: Filled with knowledge that only comes from a life fully lived, The Correspondent is a gem of a novel about the power of finding solace in literature and connection with people we might never meet in person. It is about the hubris of youth and the wisdom of old age, and the mistakes and acts of kindness that occur during a lifetime. Sybil Van Antwerp has throughout her life used letters to make sense of the world and her place in it. Most mornings, around half past ten, Sybil sits down to write letters—to her brother, to her best friend, to the president of the university who will not allow her to audit a class she desperately wants to take, to Joan Didion and Larry McMurtry to tell them what she thinks of their latest books, and to one person to whom she writes often yet never sends the letter. Sybil expects her world to go on as it always has—a mother, grandmother, wife, divorcee, distinguished lawyer, she has lived a very full life. But when letters from someone in her past force her to examine one of the most painful periods of her life, she realizes that the letter she has been writing over the years needs to be read and that she cannot move forward until she finds it in her heart to offer forgiveness. Sybil Van Antwerp’s life of letters might be “a very small thing,” but she also might be one of the most memorable characters you will ever read.

November 11 | 1-2PM

Topic: Holiday & Winter Content That Connects
Join Zoe from Moe Socials for Social Media Power Hour to learn how to create holiday and winter content that fits your business, connects with your audience, and gives people a reason to engage.
We’ll explore new trends, brainstorm fresh ideas, and share practical tips to take your content from “What should I post?” to a plan you can put into action for December.
